title: RomanSetu: Efficiently unlocking multilingual capabilities of Large Language Models via Romanization
what_it_does: Uses romanized text as the interface for extending English-centric LLMs to non-Roman-script languages via continual pretraining and instruction tuning on romanized Indic data.
key_results: Romanization reduces token fertility 2x-4x vs native script and matches or outperforms native-script representation on NLU/NLG/MT; romanized embeddings align more closely with English.
drawbacks: Requires continual pretraining (not applicable to closed judges off-the-shelf); evaluates task accuracy on clean machine-transliterated text, not noisy user romanization.
gap_vs_ours: Studies romanization as an input strategy for task performance; never asks whether an LLM evaluator assigns different quality scores to identical content in romanized vs native script.

title: Script Gap: Evaluating LLM Triage on Indian Languages in Native vs Romanized Scripts in a Real World Setting
what_it_does: Benchmarks LLMs on real user maternal-health triage queries in 5 Indian languages plus Nepali, comparing classification reliability on native vs romanized versions of the same messages.
key_results: Consistent degradation on romanized input, gaps up to 24 points across languages and models; projects ~2M excess triage errors at the partner org; proposes uncertainty-based selective routing.
drawbacks: Single classification task in one deployment context; may not generalize to open-ended generation or subjective quality assessment.
gap_vs_ours: Closest prior work; measures the LLM's own task accuracy on romanized input, not bias in an LLM-as-judge's scoring of content quality across scripts.

title: RomanLens: The Role Of Latent Romanization In Multilinguality In LLMs
what_it_does: Mechanistic interpretability (logit lens, activation patching) showing LLMs processing non-Roman-script languages represent target words in romanized form in intermediate layers.
key_results: Semantic concepts encoded similarly across native and romanized representations; romanization acts as a latent bridge for cross-lingual transfer.
drawbacks: Internal-representation findings do not quantify behavioral output differences from script choice.
gap_vs_ours: Explains why scripts may be processed asymmetrically inside the model but not whether that surfaces as score differences when the LLM judges.

title: Breaking the Script Barrier in Multilingual Pre-Trained Language Models with Transliteration-Based Post-Training Alignment
what_it_does: Transliteration-based post-pretraining alignment mapping different writing systems into Latin script to improve cross-lingual transfer between related languages.
key_results: Up to 50% improvement on some downstream tasks in English-centric transfer; larger gains from non-English sources.
drawbacks: Targets encoder-style multilingual PLMs, not instruction-tuned generative LLMs used in evaluation pipelines.
gap_vs_ours: Treats script mismatch as a transfer obstacle to fix via training; does not consider script as a bias source in judge scoring.

title: Romanization-based Large-scale Adaptation of Multilingual Language Models
what_it_does: Systematic study of UROMAN transliteration as a large-scale adaptation strategy for multilingual PLMs on 14 low-resource languages.
key_results: UROMAN-based transliteration strong for many languages; largest gains on unseen scripts and low-data setups.
drawbacks: mBERT/XLM-R-era models on classification tasks; UROMAN output differs from real user romanization (Hinglish spelling variation).
gap_vs_ours: Frames romanization as a capability booster for adaptation; no analysis of evaluation-time scoring fairness across scripts.

title: Aksharantar: Open Indic-language Transliteration datasets and models for the Next Billion Users
what_it_does: Largest public transliteration dataset for Indian languages (26M pairs, 21 languages, 12 scripts) plus the IndicXlit transliteration model.
key_results: IndicXlit improves transliteration accuracy 15% over baselines on Dakshina; first public baselines for 7 languages.
drawbacks: Resource/model paper for the transliteration task itself, not a study of downstream LLM behavior.
gap_vs_ours: Supplies tooling to build our paired stimuli but contains no analysis of judge bias across scripts.

title: COMI-LINGUA: Expert Annotated Large-Scale Dataset for Multitask NLP in Hindi-English Code-Mixing
what_it_does: 125K+ instance triple-annotated Hindi-English code-mixed dataset covering five NLP tasks in both Devanagari and Roman script variants; benchmarks LLMs on it.
key_results: Closed-source LLMs beat traditional tools zero-shot; fine-tuning reaches up to 95.25 F1 on NER, 98.77 F1 on matrix-language ID.
drawbacks: Evaluates LLMs as task performers on code-mixed data; Hindi-English only.
gap_vs_ours: Shows LLMs can process Hinglish in both scripts for NLP tasks but never tests whether a judge rates identical content differently by script.

title: CodeMixBench: Evaluating Code-Mixing Capabilities of LLMs Across 18 Languages
what_it_does: Code-mixing benchmark of eight tasks across 18 languages in seven families, with a synthetic data pipeline (word substitution + GPT-4 prompting).
key_results: LLMs consistently underperform on code-mixed data, especially across language families; data, scale, and few-shot prompting partially close the gap.
drawbacks: Relies on synthetic code-mixed text that may not reflect natural Hinglish spelling variability.
gap_vs_ours: Measures LLM competence at handling code-mixed input, not the fairness of an LLM grader when the same answer appears code-mixed/romanized vs native.
